title: Disable dormant users
product: Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory
use_case: When Sophos ITDR flags a user as dormant, disable the account where it's managed: in on-premises Active Directory, or in Entra ID for a cloud-only user.
trigger: Platform Events, source Identity Findings, event Created only. Set When does this playbook run? to Only When, with inputs.identityFindings.new.check.category.toLower() == 'dormant_resource' && inputs.identityFindings.new.primaryReference.derivedType == 'USER'
connections: Taegis.LDAP 1.0.13, the Microsoft Active Directory/LDAP connector Sophos manages, through the On-Premise Automation Connector on a data collector, to disable on-premises and synced accounts
Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to look users up and disable cloud-only accounts
requires: Sophos ITDR with Microsoft Entra ID or on-premises Active Directory connected, Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations, and for on-premises accounts a Sophos data collector that reaches a domain controller over LDAPS
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does. It disables accounts, and one can belong to a user MDR is investigating, so tell your MDR contact before you turn it on.
rollback: Enable User: enable the account again in Active Directory, or in Entra ID for a cloud-only user, and add it to Excluded users so a later finding doesn't disable it again.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook disables a user that Sophos ITDR flags as dormant: in on-premises Active Directory for on-premises and synced accounts, and in Entra ID for cloud-only accounts. A new dormant identity finding starts it, and it calls the LDAP and Microsoft Graph API connectors Sophos manages, with dry run on and only the domains you list in scope. It needs Sophos ITDR and, for on-premises accounts, a Sophos data collector that reaches a domain controller.
notes:
Setup:
- ITDR's dormant threshold is fixed: 90 days without a sign-in for Dormant Accounts, and 180 days for the Active Directory check. Posture Check Preferences only turns checks on or off.
- A 30-day rule needs a custom scheduled playbook that finds inactive users itself, for example with the Microsoft Graph API connector's searchUser function. That's untested, and the LDAP connector looks up one user at a time.
- The trigger is Created only, so findings that exist before you turn it on don't start a run. Find those with the Directory's Is Dormant filter.
- There's no approval step. Dry run, Domains and Excluded users are the controls.

How it works:
- It looks the user up in Entra ID by the finding's object ID, or by user principal name. A synced user is then looked up in Active Directory by its on-premises name, and a user Entra ID doesn't have by the finding's user principal name.
- On-premises and synced accounts are disabled in Active Directory only. Active Directory is the source of authority under Entra Connect Sync, so a disable in Entra ID alone can be undone at the next sync, while the Active Directory disable reaches Entra ID at that sync. Cloud-only accounts are disabled in Entra ID.
- An Active Directory account counts as a match only when its user principal name, sAMAccountName or mail is exactly the name looked up.
- It never disables a user ITDR flags as an admin, or an account with adminCount set.
- Identity findings take no comments, so the result is the execution's outcome under Playbooks > Executions.

Testing:
- Not run in a tenant yet.
- On 2026-11-02 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant, and a renamed copy imported, exported again unchanged apart from the tenant's own fields, and was deleted.
- The check titles and the DORMANT_RESOURCE category come from that tenant's ITDR checks. It had no identity provider connected, so it had no real dormant finding.
- Every step ran in Sophos Fusion's CEL engine, through its evaluateExpr API, against 26 made-up findings and connector replies: cloud-only, synced, on-premises only, excluded, admin, out of scope, already disabled, refused and not found.

Known gaps:
- A real dormant finding is untested. The playbook reads it through the documented finding macros, which return an empty list for a field the event lacks. A finding with no user principal name or object ID ends in FAIL.
- Whether Dormant Accounts covers on-premises Active Directory users is undocumented. The Active Directory check covers them.
- Whether the LDAP connector returns userAccountControl and adminCount is untested. Without them, the already-disabled and adminCount checks don't apply.
- Whether you can save the playbook without a connection for a directory you don't have is untested.
- There's no daily cap. A newly connected directory can create many dormant findings at once, and each run disables one user.
